ALLEGATION_ITEM_QUOTE: **The converse of claim 1 fails, and that is the subject of the next item.** A compact subset of an arbitrary space need not be closed; it is closed as soon as the ambient space is Hausdorff ([[thm-compact-subset-of-a-hausdorff-space-is-closed]]), and [[fs-a-compact-subset-is-closed-in-every-space]] records the failure without that hypothesis.
ALLEGATION_TARGET_QUOTE: The page order is “thm-compact-iff-fip, thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact, thm-compact-subset-of-a-hausdorff-space-is-closed”. The actual next item states: “3. **Compact implies closed.** Every compact subset of $X$ is closed in $X$.”
ALLEGATION_REASONING: The judge reversed the local reading order. The finite-intersection-property theorem immediately precedes the audited item; the compact-subset-of-a-Hausdorff-space theorem immediately follows it. That next theorem explicitly proves the converse direction under the Hausdorff hypothesis, while the linked false-statement item supplies the failure without that hypothesis. The Remark accurately describes both the order and the mathematics.
